js.Variación porcentual entre dos períodos: Percentage change between two selectable periods. Designed for year-on-year analysis.
js.El usuario selecciona el KPI a analizar;: The user selects the KPI to analyse; the visual adapts dynamically.
js.Técnica para destacar elementos en un vi: A technique for highlighting items in a visual without removing the context of the rest.

js.Dos productos año a año, con zoom por tr: Two products year by year, with a quarterly zoom
js.Gráfico de líneas que compara dos produc: A line chart comparing two products by year. When you select a year it’s highlighted and its quarterly breakdown appears automatically, with a label summing up what happened. You see when one overtakes the other and when the trend changes.
js.Columnas que explican cuánto cambió y cu: Columns that explain how much changed and which year was best
js.Gráfico de evolución anual con un toolti: A yearly trend chart with a tooltip that explains the change from the previous period and an automatic label on the best year. It uses native parameters to switch what’s analysed. You understand how the business evolved without opening a single table.
js.Qué productos cumplen el objetivo y cuál: Which products hit target and which need action
js.Dashboard que muestra el cumplimiento de: A dashboard that shows each product’s progress against target and classifies it: on target, below, or needs immediate action. In seconds you know where to act without comparing figures one by one. Useful for sales targets and catalogue control.
js.Tú eliges la fecha de referencia y el pe: You choose the reference date and the period to compare
js.Eliges una fecha, un periodo (30, 90, 18: Choose a date, a period (30, 90, 180 or 365 days, or year to date) and a metric. The visual works out where the comparison starts, highlights that range and shows the change in € and %, in green or red depending on the result.
js.Ventas por producto que destacan solo lo: Sales by product that highlight only what matters
js.Gráfico de ventas por producto en el que: A sales-by-product chart where you choose how many to highlight (Top N with RANKX). The top ones stay in the foreground and the rest step back. Looking at two bars instead of ten makes it much easier to decide where to act.
js.Cuando un producto aplasta la escala del: When one product squashes the chart’s scale
js.Si un producto vende mucho más que el re: If one product sells far more than the rest, the other bars look the same even when they aren’t. This visual adds a zoom using 4 DAX measures and layered charts: you see the real size of the dominant product and, at the same time, the differences between all the others. No paid visuals.
js.Evolución, variación, peso y ranking de: Trend, change, share and ranking for each product in one block
js.Un minigráfico de pendiente por producto: One slope mini chart per product that brings together its trend between two periods, the change, its % of the total and its ranking position. One click switches from units to revenue and you see how the ranking changes. All native.
js.Top N de clientes y país desde un único: Top N customers and country from a single Input Slicer
js.Gráfico de ventas por cliente controlado: A sales-by-customer chart controlled from Power BI’s new Input Slicer: you choose how many customers to highlight and from which country, and the chart highlights your selection. Titles and subtitles rewrite themselves based on what you pick.
js.Escribes el KPI que quieres ver y la tar: Type the KPI you want and the card changes
js.Tarjeta KPI con un Input Slicer: escribe: A KPI card with an Input Slicer: you type, for example, “sales + yoy” or “margin + budget” and the card shows that calculation in the right format (€, % or number). It understands Spanish and English synonyms such as “revenue” or “facturación”. Works with sales, margin, average ticket and their comparisons.
js.Busca clientes por país sin perder al re: Find customers by country without losing sight of the rest
js.Tabla de clientes en la que escribes un: A customer table where you type a country into an Input Slicer and its customers are highlighted with conditional formatting, while the others stay visible. That way you know whether those customers matter to the business or are just anecdotal. Built with Input Slicer, DAX and conditional formatting.
js.Cronograma de proyectos sin visuals exte: Project timeline with no external visuals
js.Un diagrama de Gantt hecho solo con visu: A Gantt chart built only with native visuals and DAX: one bar per task with its status, a “today” line that moves on its own, a project filter and tooltips with the details. At a glance you see what’s done, what’s still active and what’s running late. It also works for campaigns, onboarding or delivery planning.
js.Top N de proyectos con narrativa automát: Top N projects with automatic narrative
js.Visual que muestra cuánto del presupuest: A visual that shows how much of the total budget goes to the biggest projects. You choose Top 1, 3 or 5 and a DAX-generated sentence explains the result. Useful for spotting early when investment depends on just a few projects.
js.¿El presupuesto está concentrado o equil: Is the budget concentrated or balanced?
js.Widget que reparte la inversión entre pr: A widget that splits investment across projects and highlights the 1, 3 or 5 that weigh the most, with an automatic DAX sentence saying whether the budget is concentrated or balanced. Use it to spot dependency risks before they grow and explain them without doing the maths.
js.Elige dos años y ve cuánto ha cambiado e: Pick two years and see how much the business changed
js.Gráfico de columnas en el que selecciona: A column chart where you select two years and the % change between them appears. Only the two compared columns are highlighted, the rest fade out, and a label explains whether there was growth or a drop. Nobody has to do the maths to understand the trend.
js.Beneficio, unidades y margen en un visua: Profit, units and margin in one visual you steer
js.Dashboard en el que los segmentadores el: A dashboard where the slicers choose what to analyse: profit, units sold or margin %, by year, month or day. Colours change with profit and a calendar matrix lets you drill down to daily detail. Designed so the report isn’t flooded with too many metrics at once.
js.Destaca unos proyectos sin perder de vis: Spotlight some projects without losing sight of the rest
js.Al seleccionar uno o varios proyectos, s: When you select one or more projects they’re highlighted in the chart, but the others stay visible, so you keep the context of the total budget. In the example, a single project takes almost a quarter of the total and it jumps out. Works for market share, late-paying customers or project tracking.
js.Ventas mensuales con la variación % enci: Monthly sales with the % change above each bar
js.Gráfico de ventas por mes que muestra so: A monthly sales chart that shows above each bar how much it changed from the previous month, with automatic colours for rises and falls and a flag on the biggest jumps. It works with any slicer (region, campaign, product) and needs no helper tables.
js.Qué meses cumplen el objetivo y por cuán: Which months hit the target, and by how much
js.Gráfico de beneficio mensual con un obje: A monthly profit chart with a target you can adjust. Each bar shows its % of target, the months that reach it are coloured, and the target line and annual average are always visible. The subtitle rewrites itself with how many months hit the goal.
js.Cada producto comparado con su propia me: Each product compared with its own average
js.Un minigráfico por producto con la línea: One mini chart per product with a line for its average, so you know whether it’s above or below its usual level instead of comparing it with bigger products. Picking a month highlights it in every chart and a label shows the difference in units and %.
